title: Positive-degree affine-curve cohomological range
statement: Let k₀ be a finite field, l a prime different from its characteristic, and X a separated finite-type k₀-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let G be a constructible Weil sheaf [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] on X. Assume X is affine and smooth of relative dimension one over k₀, and let r be an integer greater than two. The r-th Weil cohomology sheaf of the compactly supported derived direct image [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] of G, placed in degree zero, along X → Spec k₀ is zero.

source.place: The corresponding positive-degree part of the blueprint proof

proof.text: On the geometric fibre, smoothness of relative dimension one gives a finite disjoint union of smooth connected curves. Choose a smooth proper compactification on each component. Compactification independence computes compact support by proper direct image after exact extension by zero. The empty scheme gives zero.

Choose a constructible integral lattice over a finite coefficient field. The finite reductions of its extension by zero are constructible degree-zero sheaves on a proper smooth curve. The torsion etale cohomological-dimension bound and finite-coefficient etale/pro-etale comparison give zero cohomology above degree two. Proper finiteness makes every cohomology group of each finite reduction finite.

Compute adic direct image by the derived inverse limit. For r > 2, the Milnor exact sequence has zero limit of the degree-r groups. Its first derived limit of the degree-(r-1) groups is also zero by the Mittag--Leffler theorem for finite groups; in particular this handles r = 3, where degree-two groups may be nonzero. Exact rationalization and scalar extension preserve vanishing. Forgetting the Weil structure commutes with the derived functors and reflects zero objects, giving the asserted Weil cohomology sheaf vanishing.
